(ANOC) is the Coordinating/Managing Entity (C/ME) of the project.
ANOC is a Senegalese private company owned by the Italian Bioenergy Production s.r.l.
In Senegal its activities started in 2008 with the development of first nurseries in several villages and made first pilot Jatropha plantations near Ourour (Fatic region) and Kaffrine (Kaffrine region).

1.2 Sectoral Scope and Project Type
The project is a Voluntary Carbon Standard (VCS) project within the sectoral scope of Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use (AFOLU) and category Afforestation, Reforestation and Revegetation (ARR).
The project is a grouped project.

The planned agro-forestry system will assure a proper management of trees in cultivated lands allowing the carbon storage by plants biomass and soils, consequently providing a contribution to the greenhouse effect mitigation and the reversal of soil degradation trend.
African National Oil Corporation s.a.r.l.
(ANOC) has concessions for the project lands and will be the owner of Jatropha plants and products.
Moreover, ANOC will manage the agricultural operations (e.g., sowing, fertilizing).

15. Life on land.summary: The evidence provided does not directly measure the indicator variable of forest areas managed sustainably for forest products, including sustainably produced fuelwood. The context mentions various parameters and data units related to forest management, but does not provide a direct answer to the question of total area of forest under sustainable management practices in hectares. The document MONIT_REP_1071_03JUN2009_02JUN2013.pdf mentions area values such as 344.04 ha and 571.33 ha, but these appear to be specific to certain strata or project instances and do not directly measure the indicator variable. Therefore, the evidence fails to satisfy the measurement requirement.

The annual increment in above-ground biomass stock is reported as 1.2 t d.m. ha-1 yr-1 (Document: MONIT_REP_1071_03JUN2009_02JUN2013.pdf, Page: 12), but this does not directly measure the indicator variable. The evidence fails to satisfy the measurement requirement due to the lack of explicit quantitative data directly measuring the total above and below ground biomass stock.

The aims of this project are: 
The sequestration of carbon dioxide (CO2) through the nurturing of Jatropha curcas.

The regeneration of degraded soils, protecting them against erosion processes and saving existing carbon stocks.

The empowerment of local communities to develop sustainable agro-forestry practices.

